key_insight: Applying low-rank adaptation (LoRA-style) for targeted LLM unlearning produces parameter updates that survive aggressive post-training quantization (e.g., 4-bit), avoiding the reversion to pre-unlearning behavior seen with full-parameter fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Standard full-parameter unlearning updates are often too small and get masked or erased by aggressive post-training quantization, so quantized deployments revert to their pre-unlearning behavior—this work makes unlearning robust to low-bit quantization.
method: Perform unlearning via low-rank adapters (LoRA) instead of full-parameter fine-tuning to concentrate updates in structured, higher-magnitude low-rank deltas.
Design/scale adapters and training objectives so the resulting parameter deltas are quantization-resilient (optionally combined with lightweight quantization-aware tuning).
Deploy by either keeping adapters as runtime patches or merging them into weights with a quantization-preserving merge strategy so the unlearning effect persists after PTQ.
impact: Enables compliant, privacy-preserving LLM unlearning that survives aggressive low-bit quantization, making unlearning practical for memory- and compute-constrained deployments without full model retraining or retaining full‑precision checkpoints.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained LLM → (a) full-parameter unlearning → PTQ → failure vs (b) LoRA unlearning → PTQ → success
Bar chart: unlearning retention (e.g., metric or error) across quantization bits (8-bit, 6-bit, 4-bit) comparing full-finetune vs LoRA
Heatmap or vector norm plot: magnitude/distribution of parameter deltas for full-finetune vs low-rank adapters
Icons: lock/privacy (data removal), chip/quantization (efficient inference), puzzle piece (adapter modularity)
paper_title: Quantization-Robust LLM Unlearning via Low-Rank Adaptation
paper_authors: João Vitor Boer Abitante, Joana Meneguzzo Pasquali, Luan Fonseca Garcia, Ewerton de Oliveira, Thomas da Silva Paula
